inspection_summary: Fresh whole-source inspection verified all 1046 normalized lines. The survey develops discriminant bounds as positivity-controlled explicit-formula estimates, tracks how kernel choice reallocates information from prime ideals and zeros, and connects root discriminants to class numbers, towers, Minkowski constants, regulators, and low-zero questions. Prose is coherent, but many displayed formulas and all table bodies are absent from the text layer, so formula-level claims are explicitly dependency-marked.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: states the positivity-constrained kernel method, its unconditional and GRH optimization problems, applications to conductors and class numbers, tower obstructions, empirical minima, and the field-versus-polynomial discriminant distinction

sections_inspected.label: 6. Low zeros of Dedekind zeta functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: decomposes discriminant-bound deficiency into prime-ideal and zero terms, explains an indirect computation, and studies low zeros and the conditionality gap

accepted_units.title: Eliminate inaccessible constants, then enforce sign control
accepted_units.why_material: The prose identifies the reusable move from a Hadamard-factorization identity, through elimination of hard constants and differentiated combinations, to explicit formulas whose sign constraints expose both the power and limitations of discriminant bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 58-82 supply notation; the unit begins where the analytic mechanism starts and ends after the unconditional extension and method comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed identities are absent from the text layer; retain only the strategy-level interpretation unless the scan is consulted.

accepted_units.title: Unconditional discriminant bounds as a positive-kernel extremal problem
accepted_units.why_material: The explicit formula becomes a lower-bound instrument by choosing a test function whose prime and zero contributions are nonnegative, converting analytic estimation into constrained Fourier-kernel optimization with a sharp main term and an unresolved remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span retained. For complete v2 interpretation, continue through lines 246-263, which finish the parallel GRH optimization and its remainder-term status.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core formulas are missing from extraction, but the admissibility conditions, scaling family, optimal-main-term claim, and open problems are recoverable from prose; exact constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: GRH weakens the positivity domain but not the main-term ceiling
accepted_units.why_material: Under GRH, positivity is required only through a nonnegative Fourier transform on the critical line, enlarging the admissible kernel class; nevertheless the best main term is unchanged and optimization moves to the remainder term.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the close of the carried unconditional unit to make the conditional comparison self-contained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The numerical bound and kernel display are absent; the conditionality and optimality comparison is textually explicit.

accepted_units.title: Poles obstruct transferring conductor bounds without Artin holomorphy
accepted_units.why_material: The explicit-formula method transfers from discriminants to Artin conductors only if uncontrolled pole contributions are excluded, cleanly isolating the analytic assumption that blocks an otherwise parallel argument.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained transition from kernel bounds to conductor bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete; no missing formula is needed for the obstruction.

accepted_units.title: Prescribed local completions unify discriminant and curve-genus minimization
accepted_units.why_material: Serre's local-to-global viewpoint reframes root-discriminant minimization as a problem conditioned by local completions and shows the same template turning into minimal-genus questions for curves over finite fields.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding conductor remark is not required; this is a compact conceptual transfer.

accepted_units.title: Root-discriminant invariance turns lower bounds into class-number certificates
accepted_units.why_material: Passing to the Hilbert class field preserves root discriminant while multiplying degree, so a degree-sensitive lower bound can rule out a nontrivial extension and certify class number one; weaker versions bound the class number before algebraic refinement.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the contrast with heuristic frequency and the exact Hilbert-class-field mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One degree formula is OCR-damaged, but the invariance and contradiction argument are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Infinite class-field towers defeat divergence of minimal root discriminants
accepted_units.why_material: The old conjecture that minimal root discriminants grow with degree would force all Hilbert class field towers to terminate; Golod-Shafarevich towers and Martinet sequences provide the structural obstruction and replace that expectation with bounded-root-discriminant families.
accepted_units.context_note: Exact displayed bounds are omitted, so the unit records the qualitative counterexample mechanism rather than constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed numerical bounds and one explicit field formula are missing or damaged; scan verification is required for quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: Small-discriminant data challenge degree monotonicity and expose prime-degree ignorance
accepted_units.why_material: Near-contact between analytic lower bounds and known minima supplies a calibration signal, while the degree-seven anomaly challenges monotonicity and the tower constructions' small-prime-power degrees isolate prime degree as a distinct unresolved regime.
accepted_units.context_note: The table bodies are missing, so only comparisons explicitly stated in prose are retained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on absent Tables 1-4 for numerical verification; the qualitative anomaly and prime-degree question are readable.

accepted_units.title: Field discriminants do not generally reduce to polynomial discriminants
accepted_units.why_material: Analytic field-discriminant methods do not address bounded polynomial discriminants, and equality of polynomial and field discriminants requires a power basis, a representation property expected to fail in higher degree.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the open problem, the limitation of the analytic method, and the power-basis interpretation needed to understand the gap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One discriminant value is omitted, but the representation distinction is prose-complete.

accepted_units.title: Elkies recovers a GRH-scale bound by Taylor positivity
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiated Landau-Stark identities have alternating signs under GRH; high-order Taylor truncation suppresses an unwanted pole term while preserving positivity uniformly in zero height, yielding the discriminant bound without invoking the full explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span retained as-is; its opening states the comparison target and its ending completes the epsilon-and-truncation argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Most displayed equations are absent and some symbols are damaged. The proof architecture is recoverable, but any formal or quantitative reuse requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Tailor kernels to known, absent, or targeted small prime ideals
accepted_units.why_material: Rapidly decaying general-purpose kernels can underuse known prime data; an alternative explicit-formula kernel admits termwise estimates, improves when an ideal norm is excluded, and can be redesigned to emphasize selected ideals.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the motivation and the endpoint conclusion about targeted kernel design.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel and inequalities are absent from extraction; only the design principle and stated improvement logic are safe without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Ideal-class norm bounds retain more structure than discriminant bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Geometry-of-numbers product estimates imply a small-norm representative in every ideal class and hence a discriminant bound, but the implication loses ideal-class information that remains useful for other problems.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit stops before the analytic replacement for the geometric constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed norm and discriminant inequalities are missing; the implication and information-loss comparison are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Ideal-class zeta functions improve Minkowski constants but resist GRH import
accepted_units.why_material: Zimmert's analytic use of ideal-class zeta functions strengthens small-ideal representatives and recovers an unconditional discriminant bound, yet the lack of Euler products and failure of GRH for these functions blocks a naive conditional upgrade.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the extremality question for the underlying linear forms and the stated target for further improvement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Quantitative constants are partly missing; the method, consequence, and GRH obstruction are prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Analytic regulator bounds extend the zeta-function strategy
accepted_units.why_material: Zimmert's ideal-class analytic machinery also yields regulator lower bounds, with Friedman variants improving small-degree behavior and later reformulation suggesting a path to stronger general estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: Stops before a proposed bound whose formula is absent from the normalized source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The main inequality is missing, so retain the method lineage and qualitative comparison but not an exact bound.

accepted_units.title: Discriminant-bound deficiency splits into small-prime and low-zero contributions
accepted_units.why_material: Because the explicit formula is an identity, excess discriminant over a baseline bound must be supplied by prime ideals or zeros; decay localizes the relevant terms, and zeros can be inferred by subtracting computable prime-ideal contributions when direct zero computation is unavailable.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the setup required to interpret both the numerical comparison and the carried low-zero unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The referenced explicit formula is absent, but the decomposition and subtraction protocol are fully described in prose.

accepted_units.title: Use the same kernel to compare prime and zero shares, then test kernel sensitivity
accepted_units.why_material: The survey fixes the discriminant-bound kernel, defines deficiency and prime-ideal columns, obtains the zero share by subtraction, and warns that the apparent balance shifts materially under the unconditional optimal kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Captures methodology and the stated qualitative outcome without reconstructing missing table values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table 5 values are absent; only the protocol, field panel description, and prose conclusion that shares are comparable are usable.

accepted_units.why_material: The text contrasts the lack of an algebraic small-prime guarantee with asymptotic low-zero results, then reframes the GRH gap as positivity of a kernel on different regions and sketches mixtures that tolerate broad classes of off-line zeros while exposing unusual zero distributions as the remaining obstruction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Explicit formulas as constrained information budgets
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Kernel admissibility and shape determine which zero and prime contributions can safely be discarded, emphasized, or inferred, so both bound strength and the apparent prime-versus-zero explanation are representation-dependent outputs of one constrained budgeting mechanism.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact kernels, constants, and Table 5 values are absent from the text layer, and all conclusions remain conditional on the chosen explicit-formula interface.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Root discriminant as a tower-invariant obstruction detector
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Root-discriminant invariance makes degree-sensitive lower bounds powerful enough to constrain Hilbert class fields, while infinite towers show that the same invariant also falsifies naive global growth expectations and redirects attention to restricted degree families.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The survey provides historical constructions and qualitative bounds, not a classification or a modern optimality claim.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Conditionality is a positivity-domain choice
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The gap between unconditional, GRH, and Artin-conditional bounds is organized by where transformed kernels must be nonnegative and whether poles or off-line zeros can contribute with uncontrolled sign.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The surviving prose supports this conceptual comparison, but missing formulas prevent checking the precise admissible regions and error terms.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic methods recover structure beyond a scalar discriminant
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Moving from a bare discriminant inequality to ideal-class zeta functions and regulator formulas preserves or produces information about class representatives and units that scalar discriminant bounds discard.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-survey methodological relation; the displayed constants and proposed regulator inequality require scan recovery.
